prs.title: fix(auth): match complete WWW-Authenticate parameters
prs.author: tarunag10
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs patch the exact same location in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py (right after the imports, before extract_field_from_www_auth) to fix the same bug: WWW-Authenticate header parsing was doing naive/regex substring matching on the raw header string, which can incorrectly match parameter names that are substrings of other tokens (or of quoted values) instead of properly splitting the header into distinct, quote-aware auth-param tokens on top-level commas. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs patch the exact same location in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py (right after the imports, before extract_field_from_www_auth) to fix the same bug: WWW-Authenticate header parsing was doing naive/regex substring matching on the raw header string, which can incorrectly match parameter names that are substrings of other tokens (or of quoted values) instead of properly splitting the header into distinct, quote-aware auth-param tokens on top-level commas. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #3012's diff is fully self-contained: a single helper (_iter_www_auth_params) that walks the header once, correctly handling quoted values and backslash escapes, and it deletes the now-unused `import re`, fully removing the fragile regex approach that caused the bug. PR #3041 introduces two helpers (_split_www_authenticate_segments + _extract_bearer_auth_params) with an added scheme-detection heuristic to re-associate comma-separated segments back to a specific 'Bearer' scheme; the provided diff cuts off mid-function (`if collec...`), it does not show removal of the `import re` line, and the scheme/segment-boundary heuristic is inherently more fragile since a bare comma cannot always be reliably classified as a param-separator vs. a new-challenge-separator without a full grammar (RFC 7235 ambiguity), leaving more edge cases exposed to misparsing than the simpler complete single-challenge approach in #3012.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #3012's diff is fully self-contained: a single helper (_iter_www_auth_params) that walks the header once, correctly handling quoted values and backslash escapes, and it deletes the now-unused `import re`, fully removing the fragile regex approach that caused the bug. PR #3041 introduces two helpers (_split_www_authenticate_segments + _extract_bearer_auth_params) with an added scheme-detection heuristic to re-associate comma-separated segments back to a specific 'Bearer' scheme; the provided diff cuts off mid-function (`if collec...`), it does not show removal of the `import re` line, and the scheme/segment-boundary heuristic is inherently more fragile since a bare comma cannot always be reliably classified as a param-separator vs. a new-challenge-separator without a full grammar (RFC 7235 ambiguity), leaving more edge cases exposed to misparsing than the simpler complete single-challenge approach in #3012.
